{"parentUuid":null,"isSidechain":true,"promptId":"49872cc4-d709-4ab4-ae05-cf02560ec711","agentId":"a24ebe54d96b84494","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"You are fixing TWO issues in the SIGIL Phase 9 Companion PWA (an installable web app that lets an owner's phone drive SIGIL over WireGuard). Repo /home/kali/sigil, branch `phase9-companion`. RULES: (1) touch ONLY `sigil/bridge/webapp/app.js`, `sigil/bridge/webapp/index.html`, and (if useful) add assertions to `tests/test_bridge_webapp.py`; (2) DO NOT run ANY git command; (3) run ONLY `~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_bridge_webapp.py` to verify; leave changes uncommitted.\n\nFIRST read: `sigil/bridge/webapp/app.js` (the whole client — device key, `canonicalJson`, envelope signing, approval signing, the `data-act` click delegation, `flushOutbox`, `nextNonce`), `sigil/bridge/webapp/canonical.js`, `sigil/bridge/webapp/index.html`, `sigil/gesture/session.py` (the functions `arm_request_message` + `sign_arm_request` and the constant `_ARM_CORE` — this is the EXACT contract the JS must reproduce), and `sigil/bridge/server.py` (the `POST /api/gesture/arm` endpoint — the body IS the device-signed credential, like `/api/action`; no envelope wrapper).\n\nFIX 1 — LOW-8 (outbox silently drops a refused emergency-stop). `flushOutbox` currently re-sends each queued already-signed POST and `idbDel`s it as soon as the fetch RESOLVES with ANY status — so a `panic`/`relay` the owner tapped offline, flushed >120s later and refused as stale (409/401), is deleted and never re-surfaced. Fix: on flush, inspect the response status; if a queued POST comes back NON-OK (>=400), do NOT silently delete it — surface an explicit, visible \"delivery FAILED — re-tap\" banner/state (especially for panic, an emergency stop), and either keep it for manual retry or clearly mark it failed. A successful (2xx) flush deletes as today. Make the failure honestly visible in the UI, not swallowed.\n\nFIX 2 — HIGH-3 (the phone cannot actually ARM a gesture session — the feature is inert end-to-end). Add an \"Arm gesture session\" control (a button in `index.html` with a `data-act` value, wired in app.js's existing click delegation — NO inline handlers, strict CSP `default-src 'self'`). When tapped it must:\n- Build the arm-request core EXACTLY as `sign_arm_request` does: `core = {signal:\"gesture.arm_request\", device_id:<this device's id>, nonce:<a fresh int nonce>, ts:<Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)>, ttl_seconds:120}`. (Use the device_id the pairing panel already generates; use a fresh monotonic nonce — reuse/extend the existing nonce counter so it's an int, and DISTINCT per arm since the server refuses a replayed (device,nonce).)\n- Sign `canonicalJson(core)` with the device's WebCrypto Ed25519 key (the SAME key + signing path used for approvals), producing a base64 `sig` with the SAME encoding approvals use (standard base64 with padding — matches Python `verify_one`).\n- POST the body `{...core, pubkey:<device pubkey b64>, sig}` to `/api/gesture/arm` (the body is the credential; no `X-SIGIL-Envelope`). Show the JSON result (`{ok,seq}` or the error) honestly in the UI.\n- IMPORTANT context to surface in the UI copy: arming only RECORDS a signed request; the PC's gesture daemon re-verifies and actually arms it — so the button confirms \"arm request sent\", and the owner should understand the PC still enforces freshness/kill-switch/single-session/TTL. Keep the copy honest (don't claim it definitely armed).\n\nVERIFY the canonical parity: `canonicalJson({signal:\"gesture.arm_request\",device_id:\"phone1\",nonce:1,ts:1700000000,ttl_seconds:120})` in JS must equal Python `sigil.gesture.session.arm_request_message` of the same core (which selects only the `_ARM_CORE` keys, all present here). Add this to `tests/test_bridge_webapp.py` as a node-vs-Python parity assertion (the file already runs `canonical.js` via node — extend it), skip-if-node-absent. Also keep the existing CSP-safety assertions passing (no inline handlers, no external origins).\n\nRun `~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_bridge_webapp.py` until all-pass. Final report: what you changed in each file, the arm-request JS you added, the parity result, and any deviation. Leave everything UNCOMMITTED."},"uuid":"9af1a0fd-ac77-4bd2-acdf-14a2f881d038","timestamp":"2026-07-19T05:27:39.301Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

The JS<->Python PARITY CONTRACT.\n3\t *\n4\t * Byte-identical to Python (sigil/reuse/canonical.py :: canonical_json):\n5\t *     json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(\",\",\":\"), ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")\n6\t * This is the #1 correctness item: the desktop bridge verifies the device signature over\n7\t * exactly these bytes (sigil/bridge/envelope.py :: envelope_message), so the phone MUST\n8\t * reproduce them or every signature is rejected.\n9\t *\n10\t * PINNED PARITY VECTOR (from tests/test_bridge_envelope.py ::\n11\t *   test_envelope_message_fixed_vector_parity):\n12\t *     core = {\"v\":1,\"device\":\"DEVKEYB64\",\"action\":\"read:snapshot\",\"args\":{},\"nonce\":1,\"ts\":1700000000}\n13\t *     canonicalJson(core)  ===  the UTF-8 bytes of the string\n14\t *     {\"action\":\"read:snapshot\",\"args\":{},\"device\":\"DEVKEYB64\",\"nonce\":1,\"ts\":1700000000,\"v\":1}\n15\t *\n16\t * Why plain JSON.stringify is safe for the LEAVES: over the SIGIL value domain — ASCII object\n17\t * keys; strings; INTEGER numbers only (app.js floors ts to whole seconds and uses integer\n18\t * nonces / seqs — floats are NEVER signed, because float repr can diverge between the two\n19\t * runtimes); booleans; null; arrays — ECMAScript JSON.stringify emits bytes identical to Python\n20\t * json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False): the same string escapes (\\\" \\\\ \\b \\t \\n \\f \\r, all other\n21\t * control chars as lowercase \\u00xx, non-ASCII left raw, \"/\" NOT escaped), the same integer\n22\t * rendering, and the same true/false/null tokens. The ONLY two things json.dumps does that plain\n23\t * JSON.stringify does not are (1) recursive KEY SORTING and (2) the compact \",\"/\":\" separators\n24\t * with no spaces — which is precisely, and only, what this function adds.\n25\t *\n26\t * Exported for BOTH the browser (window.SigilCanonical) and Node (module.exports) so the parity\n27\t * is falsifiable: tests/test_bridge_webapp.py runs this exact function under Node and asserts the\n28\t * bytes equal Python's envelope_message for the fixed vector.\n29\t */\n30\t(function (root, factory) {\n31\t  var api = factory();\n32\t  if (typeof module !== \"undefined\" && module.exports) { module.exports = api; }   // Node\n33\t  else { root.SigilCanonical = api; }                                              // browser / worker\n34\t})(typeof self !== \"undefined\" ? self : this, function () {\n35\t  function canonicalJson(value) {\n36\t    if (value === null || typeof value !== \"object\") {\n37\t      // string / number / boolean / null — JSON.stringify matches Python for the SIGIL domain\n38\t      return JSON.stringify(value);\n39\t    }\n40\t    if (Array.isArray(value)) {\n41\t      var parts = [];\n42\t      for (var i = 0; i < value.length; i++) { parts.push(canonicalJson(value[i])); }\n43\t      return \"[\" + parts.join(\",\") + \"]\";\n44\t    }\n45\t    // object: sort keys (code-unit order == Unicode code-point order for ASCII keys), compact\n46\t    var keys = Object.keys(value).sort();\n47\t    var out = \"\";\n48\t    for (var j = 0; j < keys.length; j++) {\n49\t      var k = keys[j];\n50\t      if (j) { out += \",\"; }\n51\t      out += JSON.stringify(k) + \":\" + canonicalJson(value[k]);\n52\t    }\n53\t    return \"{\" + out + \"}\";\n54\t  }\n55\t  return { canonicalJson: canonicalJson };\n56\t});\n57\t"}]},"uuid":"70185603-7ea8-4460-9254-1b2a6c3f0ce3","timestamp":"2026-07-19T05:27:43.653Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"39af2f6c-e9a9-48be-a040-a99b4f5e3740","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"9c8b982c-e1ac-4ce8-9817-f07b3e3b5593","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"49872cc4-d709-4ab4-ae05-cf02560ec711","agentId":"a24ebe54d96b84494","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011sJR9Y2qXvvtskcHMvH21S","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"SessionGate (Phase 8, WS-F, THE KEYSTONE) — the ONLY authority that injects input, and only inside\n2\tan owner-armed session. Two enforcement layers so a gesture can NEVER trigger an unintended action:\n3\t\n4\t  Layer 1 — the SESSION: `arm()` REQUIRES the owner key (it cannot be armed without the owner\n5\t  identity) and appends a signed `gesture.session_armed` record — the tamper-evident AUDIT proof-of-\n6\t  authorization, indicator-lit. The INJECTION gate itself is the live in-memory session, held ONLY by\n7\t  the owner's own running daemon process; it is BOUNDED by a TTL and ended by disarm / hand-loss /\n8\t  expiry. Injection is REFUSED with no live session.\n9\t\n10\t  Layer 2 — per intent, the tier is DERIVED from the WARDEN oracle (`hid.*` names): A1 (pointer\n11\t  move/click/scroll/drag) injects within the session; A2 (type/combo/app.launch) is QUEUED for a\n12\t  verified owner/device approval bound to `sha256(session_id|tool|args)` and NEVER auto-injected — so\n13\t  a gesture alone can never type a password or launch an app.\n14\t\n15\tOnly arm/disarm + DISCRETE actions (click/scroll/drag injected; type/launch queued) hit the spine —\n16\tper-frame pointer MOVES are telemetry (30 FPS records would DoS the append-only log).\"\"\"\n17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n18\t\n19\timport math\n20\timport time\n21\timport uuid\n22\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n23\tfrom typing import Optional\n24\t\n25\t_KS_CACHE_TTL = 0.5    # bound the per-intent kill-switch consult to ≤2 spine scans/sec (never per-frame at 30fps)\n26\t\n27\tfrom ..agents.base import Tier\n28\tfrom ..reuse import sha256_hex\n29\tfrom .components import InputBackend\n30\tfrom .types import GestureIntent\n31\t\n32\tSESSION_ARMED = \"gesture.session_armed\"\n33\tSESSION_DISARMED = \"gesture.session_disarmed\"\n34\tACTION_SIGNAL = \"gesture.action\"\n35\tARM_REQUEST = \"gesture.arm_request\"\n36\t\n37\tMAX_DEVICE_TTL = 300.0        # a DEVICE-armed session is deliberately SHORTER than a local owner arm (1800)\n38\tARM_FRESHNESS = 30.0          # a device arm request must be recent (anti-stale / bounds the replay window)\n39\t_ARM_CORE = (\"signal\", \"device_id\", \"nonce\", \"ts\", \"ttl_seconds\")\n40\t\n41\tINTENT_TOOL = {\n42\t    \"move\": \"hid.pointer.move\", \"click\": \"hid.pointer.click\",\n43\t    \"scroll_left\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\", \"scroll_right\": \"hid.pointer.scroll\",\n44\t    \"drag\": \"hid.pointer.drag\", \"type\": \"hid.type\", \"combo\": \"hid.combo\", \"launch\": \"hid.app.launch\",\n45\t}\n46\t\n47\t\n48\tdef pending_device_arm(store, trusted_pubkey=None):\n49\t    \"\"\"The newest RECORDED device arm request (written by the bridge's `submit_arm_request`) that has NOT\n50\t    yet armed a session — a candidate for `arm_by_device`, which RE-VERIFIES it fully (auth / freshness /\n51\t    kill-switch / replay / single-session / TTL). Returns the request dict, or None. This is the wiring\n52\t    that makes the remote-arm path reachable end-to-end (the gesture daemon consumes it).\"\"\"\n53\t    armed = set()\n54\t    candidate = None\n55\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n56\t        p = r.payload\n57\t        if p.get(\"signal\") == SESSION_ARMED and p.get(\"armed_by\") == \"device\":\n58\t            armed.add((p.get(\"device_pubkey\"), p.get(\"nonce\")))\n59\t        elif (p.get(\"signal\") == ARM_REQUEST and p.get(\"decision\") == \"auto\"\n60\t              and p.get(\"sig\") and p.get(\"pubkey\")):\n61\t            candidate = dict(p)                       # newest recorded request wins (seq order)\n62\t    if candidate is None or (candidate.get(\"pubkey\"), candidate.get(\"nonce\")) in armed:\n63\t        return None\n64\t    return candidate\n65\t\n66\t\n67\tdef arm_request_message(core: dict) -> bytes:\n68\t    \"\"\"The canonical bytes a device signs to request an arm — ONLY the signed core fields, so a caller\n69\t    cannot smuggle unsigned extras. Mirrors the approval/envelope canonical-json contract.\"\"\"\n70\t    from ..reuse import canonical_json\n71\t    m = canonical_json({k: core.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE})\n72\t    return m if isinstance(m, bytes) else m.encode(\"utf-8\")\n73\t\n74\t\n75\tdef sign_arm_request(device_key, *, device_id: str, nonce, ts: float, ttl_seconds: float) -> dict:\n76\t    \"\"\"Phone-side: build a device-signed arm request. The device signs with its OWN key (never the owner\n77\t    trust-root); the owner authorized this device once via the mesh ledger. This is the credential the\n78\t    bridge records and `SessionGate.arm_by_device` verifies.\"\"\"\n79\t    from ..reuse import sign\n80\t    core = {\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"device_id\": device_id, \"nonce\": nonce, \"ts\": ts, \"ttl_seconds\": ttl_seconds}\n81\t    return {**core, \"pubkey\": device_key.public_key_b64,\n82\t            \"sig\": sign(device_key.private_key_b64, arm_request_message(core))}\n83\t\n84\t\n85\t@dataclass\n86\tclass Session:\n87\t    session_id: str\n88\t    live: bool = True\n89\t    expires_at: float = 0.0            # wallclock deadline — a session is BOUNDED, never indefinite\n90\t\n91\t    def expired(self, now: float) -> bool:\n92\t        return self.expires_at > 0.0 and now >= self.expires_at\n93\t\n94\t\n95\tclass SessionGate:\n96\t    def __init__(self, store, backend: InputBackend, *, classifier=None, owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey=None):\n97\t        self.store = store\n98\t        self.backend = backend\n99\t        self._classifier = classifier\n100\t        self._owner_key = owner_key\n101\t        self._trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey\n102\t        self.session: Optional[Session] = None\n103\t        self._ks_engaged = False\n104\t        self._ks_checked_at = -1e9        # forces a fresh check on the first consult\n105\t\n106\t    def _trusted(self):\n107\t        if self._trusted_pubkey is None:\n108\t            from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n109\t            self._trusted_pubkey = owner_pubkey()\n110\t        return self._trusted_pubkey\n111\t\n112\t    def _killswitch_engaged(self, now: float) -> bool:\n113\t        \"\"\"Kill-switch state, cached for ≤_KS_CACHE_TTL so a 30fps `handle` loop does not re-scan the\n114\t        append-only spine per frame (that scan is O(spine) — a self-DoS). Panic latency is bounded by\n115\t        the TTL. The arm path checks the kill-switch FRESH (uncached), so arming can never race a halt.\"\"\"\n116\t        if now - self._ks_checked_at >= _KS_CACHE_TTL:\n117\t            from ..governor.killswitch import KillSwitch\n118\t            self._ks_engaged = KillSwitch(self.store).is_engaged()\n119\t            self._ks_checked_at = now\n120\t        return self._ks_engaged\n121\t\n122\t    def _cls(self):\n123\t        if self._classifier is None:\n124\t            from ..agents.kernel_classify import KernelClassifier\n125\t            self._classifier = KernelClassifier()\n126\t        return self._classifier\n127\t\n128\t    # --- Layer 1: the owner-armed session ---------------------------------------------------------\n129\t    def arm(self, *, owner_key=None, ttl_seconds: float = 1800.0) -> Session:\n130\t        from ..governor.authn import signed_payload\n131\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_keypair\n132\t        ok = owner_key if owner_key is not None else (self._owner_key or owner_keypair())\n133\t        if ok is None:\n134\t            raise RuntimeError(\"cannot arm a gesture session without the owner key (BLOCK-3)\")\n135\t        sid = uuid.uuid4().hex\n136\t        core = {\"signal\": SESSION_ARMED, \"session_id\": sid}\n137\t        self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n138\t                          payload={**signed_payload(core, ok), \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\",\n139\t                                   \"ttl_seconds\": ttl_seconds,\n140\t                                   \"summary\": \"gesture session ARMED (indicator lit — opt-in)\"})\n141\t        self.session = Session(sid, live=True, expires_at=time.time() + ttl_seconds)\n142\t        return self.session\n143\t\n144\t    def disarm(self) -> None:\n145\t        if self.session is not None:\n146\t            self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n147\t                              payload={\"signal\": SESSION_DISARMED, \"session_id\": self.session.session_id,\n148\t                                       \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\", \"summary\": \"gesture session DISARMED\"})\n149\t            self.session.live = False\n150\t        self.session = None\n151\t\n152\t    # --- Layer 1b: DEVICE-signed remote arm (a deliberate, reviewed trust-widening) ----------------\n153\t    def arm_by_device(self, request: dict, *, now: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[Session]:\n154\t        \"\"\"Arm on a VERIFIED, owner-authorized DEVICE signature (SIGIL §remote-arm). Every downstream\n155\t        bound is UNCHANGED — the A1-inject/A2-queue tier gate, the TTL, hand-loss/expiry disarm, and an\n156\t        owner disarm/kill that always wins. Fail-closed at each step; a refusal is recorded, never armed.\"\"\"\n157\t        from ..governor.killswitch import KillSwitch\n158\t        from ..mesh import authorized_devices\n159\t        from ..reuse import verify_one\n160\t        now = time.time() if now is None else now\n161\t        # (1) kill-switch FIRST — an owner halt (incl. a phone panic) beats any arm.\n162\t        if KillSwitch(self.store).is_engaged():\n163\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"kill-switch engaged\")\n164\t        # (2) owner-minted device key + valid signature over the signed core (RP-APPROVAL-2: the\n165\t        #     authorized set is owner-signed only, so a merely-presented key is never trusted).\n166\t        if request.get(\"signal\") != ARM_REQUEST:\n167\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"not an arm request\")\n168\t        pub = request.get(\"pubkey\")\n169\t        authorized = authorized_devices(self.store, self._trusted())\n170\t        core = {k: request.get(k) for k in _ARM_CORE}\n171\t        try:                                            # verify_one RAISES on a malformed-length sig — treat as refusal\n172\t            sig_ok = bool(pub) and pub in authorized and verify_one(pub, arm_request_message(core), request.get(\"sig\", \"\"))\n173\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — any crypto/decoding error is a fail-closed refusal, never a crash\n174\t            sig_ok = False\n175\t        if not sig_ok:\n176\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"unauthorized or invalid device signature\")\n177\t        # (3) freshness — bounds the replay window and rejects a stale captured request. Written\n178\t        #     fail-CLOSED for non-finite input: `nan > 30` is False, so a signed NaN ts would slip a\n179\t        #     `>`-style gate; require finite AND within-window explicitly.\n180\t        try:\n181\t            ts = float(request.get(\"ts\"))\n182\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n183\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"missing/invalid timestamp\")\n184\t        if not math.isfinite(ts) or not (abs(now - ts) <= ARM_FRESHNESS):\n185\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"stale or non-finite timestamp\")\n186\t        # (4) replay — this (device, nonce) must not have armed before (the append-only spine is witness).\n187\t        nonce = request.get(\"nonce\")\n188\t        for r in self.store.iter_records():\n189\t            p = r.payload\n190\t            if (p.get(\"signal\") == SESSION_ARMED and p.get(\"armed_by\") == \"device\"\n191\t                    and p.get(\"device_pubkey\") == pub and p.get(\"nonce\") == nonce):\n192\t                return self._refuse_arm(request, \"replayed arm nonce\")\n193\t        # (5) single live session — a device arm NEVER displaces an existing/owner session.\n194\t        if self.session is not None and self.session.live and not self.session.expired(now):\n195\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"a gesture session is already live\")\n196\t        # (6) TTL clamp — shorter than a local owner arm; a deliberate trust-narrowing inside the widening.\n197\t        #     Reject non-finite/non-positive BEFORE the min() (min(nan,300)=nan → a never-expiring session).\n198\t        try:\n199\t            raw_ttl = float(request.get(\"ttl_seconds\", MAX_DEVICE_TTL))\n200\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n201\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"invalid ttl\")\n202\t        if not math.isfinite(raw_ttl) or raw_ttl <= 0:\n203\t            return self._refuse_arm(request, \"non-finite or non-positive ttl\")\n204\t        ttl = min(raw_ttl, MAX_DEVICE_TTL)\n205\t        sid = uuid.uuid4().hex\n206\t        # The record's AUTHORIZATION is the verified device signature — self-verifying vs the owner-signed\n207\t        # device ledger; actor=DEVICE mirrors submit_device_approval. Store the ORIGINAL SIGNED core\n208\t        # fields (so the sig re-verifies for ANY ttl, incl. a clamped one) + the effective TTL separately,\n209\t        # and ONLY known fields (never `**request` — no unsigned extras persisted).\n210\t        self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n211\t                          payload={\"signal\": SESSION_ARMED, \"session_id\": sid, \"armed_by\": \"device\",\n212\t                                   \"device_id\": core[\"device_id\"], \"device_pubkey\": pub,\n213\t                                   \"nonce\": core[\"nonce\"], \"ts\": core[\"ts\"],\n214\t                                   \"ttl_seconds\": core[\"ttl_seconds\"],   # ORIGINAL signed value → sig re-verifies\n215\t                                   \"effective_ttl\": ttl,                 # the CLAMPED ttl actually enforced\n216\t                                   \"sig\": request.get(\"sig\"), \"pubkey\": pub, \"authorization\": \"device-signed\",\n217\t                                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\",\n218\t                                   \"summary\": \"gesture session ARMED by authorized device (remote)\"})\n219\t        self.session = Session(sid, live=True, expires_at=now + ttl)\n220\t        return self.session\n221\t\n222\t    def _refuse_arm(self, request: dict, reason: str) -> None:\n223\t        self.store.append(kind=\"refusal\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"DEVICE\",\n224\t                          payload={\"signal\": ARM_REQUEST, \"decision\": \"refused\", \"tier\": \"A0\",\n225\t                                   \"device_id\": request.get(\"device_id\"), \"reason\": reason,\n226\t                                   \"summary\": f\"device gesture arm refused: {reason}\"})\n227\t        return None\n228\t\n229\t    # --- Layer 2: per-intent tier gate ------------------------------------------------------------\n230\t    def handle(self, intent: GestureIntent) -> dict:\n231\t        \"\"\"Authorize + act on ONE intent. Returns a verdict dict. Injection ONLY inside a live session\n232\t        and ONLY for A1 tools; A2+ queues for approval and injects NOTHING; a danger name → refused.\"\"\"\n233\t        if intent.kind == \"hand_lost\":\n234\t            self.disarm()\n235\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"hand lost — session disarmed\"}\n236\t        # An owner halt (incl. a phone panic_engage) neuters injection mid-session — critical for a\n237\t        # device-armed session the owner may not be watching. Cached (≤_KS_CACHE_TTL) so a 30fps loop\n238\t        # never re-scans the spine per frame; panic latency is bounded by the TTL.\n239\t        if self._killswitch_engaged(time.time()):\n240\t            self.disarm()\n241\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"kill-switch engaged — session disarmed\"}\n242\t        if self.session is None or not self.session.live:\n243\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"no armed session — injection refused\"}\n244\t        if self.session.expired(time.time()):             # BLOCK-2: a session is bounded, never indefinite\n245\t            self.disarm()\n246\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": \"session expired — disarmed\"}\n247\t        tool = INTENT_TOOL.get(intent.kind)\n248\t        if tool is None:\n249\t            return {\"injected\": False, \"reason\": f\"unknown intent {intent.kind}\"}\n250\t        tier = self._cls().classify(tool)                 # DERIVED, fail-closed A3 on any error\n251\t        args = f\"{intent.dx:.4f},{intent.dy:.4f},{intent.arg}\"\n252\t        if tier <= Tier.A1:\n253\t            self._inject(intent)\n254\t            # BLOCK-1: log the DISCRETE A1 injections that actually take effect (click/scroll/drag);\n255\t            # per-frame `move` is telemetry (logging it at 30 FPS would DoS the append-only spine).\n256\t            if intent.kind != \"move\":\n257\t                self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n258\t                                  payload={\"signal\": ACTION_SIGNAL, \"decision\": \"auto\", \"tier\": tier.label(),\n259\t                                           \"tool\": tool, \"session_id\": self.session.session_id,\n260\t                                           \"summary\": f\"gesture {tool} injected\"})\n261\t            return {\"injected\": True, \"tier\": tier.label(), \"tool\": tool}\n262\t        # A2/A3 → QUEUE an approval bound to this exact action; inject NOTHING\n263\t        token = sha256_hex(f\"{self.session.session_id}|{tool}|{args}\".encode(\"utf-8\"))\n264\t        seq = self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"gesture\", actor=\"PERCEPTION\",\n265\t                                payload={\"signal\": ACTION_SIGNAL, \"decision\": \"queued\",\n266\t                                         \"status\": \"awaiting-approval\", \"tier\": tier.label(),\n267\t                                         \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token, \"args\": args,\n268\t                                         \"subject\": f\"gesture action {tool} (awaiting approval)\"})\n269\t        return {\"injected\": False, \"queued\": seq, \"tier\": tier.label(), \"tool\": tool, \"action_token\": token}\n270\t\n271\t    def _inject(self, intent: GestureIntent) -> None:\n272\t        b = self.backend\n273\t        if intent.kind == \"move\" or intent.kind == \"drag\":\n274\t            b.move(intent.dx, intent.dy)\n275\t        elif intent.kind == \"click\":\n276\t            b.click()\n277\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_left\":\n278\t            b.scroll(-1, 0)\n279\t        elif intent.kind == \"scroll_right\":\n280\t            b.scroll(1, 0)\n281\t"}]},"uuid":"ce3cac25-616f-48ce-9597-5f1b71b186eb","timestamp":"2026-07-19T05:27:44.608Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"9c8b982c-e1ac-4ce8-9817-f07b3e3b5593","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

It holds the phone's OWN\n3\tEd25519 device key and signs LOCALLY; the desktop bridge only verifies.\n4\t\n5\tThese tests assert three things the slice must hold:\n6\t  1. all webapp files exist and are non-empty;\n7\t  2. CSP-safety — no external origins, no inline event handlers, no inline <script> bodies (the app\n8\t     is served under a strict `default-src 'self'` CSP that would break any of those);\n9\t  3. the #1 correctness item — CANONICALIZATION PARITY: the JS `canonicalJson` (canonical.js) must\n10\t     reproduce, BYTE-FOR-BYTE, the exact signed bytes the Python bridge verifies\n11\t     (sigil.bridge.envelope.envelope_message / sigil.reuse.canonical_json). This is run under Node so\n12\t     it is falsifiable, not asserted by inspection.\n13\t\n14\tRun: ~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_bridge_webapp.py\n15\t\"\"\"\n16\timport json\n17\timport re\n18\timport shutil\n19\timport subprocess\n20\tfrom pathlib import Path\n21\t\n22\tfrom sigil.bridge import build_core, envelope_message\n23\tfrom sigil.reuse import canonical_json\n24\t\n25\tfrom sigil.bridge import envelope as _E\n26\tWEBAPP = Path(_E.__file__).parent / \"webapp\"\n27\t\n28\tFILES = [\"index.html\", \"app.js\", \"style.css\", \"manifest.json\", \"service-worker.js\", \"canonical.js\"]\n29\t\n30\t\n31\tdef _read(name):\n32\t    return (WEBAPP / name).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n33\t\n34\t\n35\t# ---- 1. every webapp file exists and is non-empty -------------------------------------------------\n36\tdef test_all_webapp_files_exist_and_nonempty():\n37\t    for name in FILES:\n38\t        p = WEBAPP / name\n39\t        assert p.is_file(), f\"missing webapp file: {name}\"\n40\t        assert p.stat().st_size > 0, f\"empty webapp file: {name}\"\n41\t\n42\t\n43\t# ---- 2a. no external origins in the JS/HTML (CSP default-src 'self') ------------------------------\n44\tdef test_no_external_origins():\n45\t    for name in (\"app.js\", \"index.html\"):\n46\t        text = _read(name)\n47\t        assert \"http://\" not in text, f\"{name} must not reference an http:// external origin\"\n48\t        assert \"https://\" not in text, f\"{name} must not reference an https:// external origin\"\n49\t\n50\t\n51\t# ---- 2b. no inline event handlers (event-delegation discipline only) -----------------------------\n52\tdef test_no_inline_event_handlers():\n53\t    for name in (\"app.js\", \"index.html\"):\n54\t        text = _read(name)\n55\t        assert \"onclick=\" not in text, f\"{name} must not use an inline onclick= handler\"\n56\t        assert \"onload=\" not in text, f\"{name} must not use an inline onload= handler\"\n57\t    # index.html: no HTML tag may carry ANY inline on*= handler attribute\n58\t    html = _read(\"index.html\")\n59\t    inline_attr = re.compile(r\"<[a-zA-Z][^>]*\\son[a-z]+\\s*=\", re.DOTALL)\n60\t    assert not inline_attr.search(html), \"index.html has an inline on*= handler attribute (CSP-unsafe)\"\n61\t\n62\t\n63\t# ---- 2c. index.html has only <script src=...> — no inline script body -----------------------------\n64\tdef test_index_scripts_are_external_only():\n65\t    html = _read(\"index.html\")\n66\t    scripts = re.findall(r\"<script\\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</script>\", html, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)\n67\t    assert scripts, \"index.html should load the app via <script src=...>\"\n68\t    for attrs, body in scripts:\n69\t        assert \"src=\" in attrs, f\"<script{attrs}> has no src= (inline script is CSP-unsafe)\"\n70\t        assert body.strip() == \"\", f\"<script{attrs}> has an inline body (CSP-unsafe): {body!r}\"\n71\t\n72\t\n73\t# ---- 2d. the JS wires behaviour via a delegated listener + holds no vendored crypto ---------------\n74\tdef test_app_uses_event_delegation_and_webcrypto_only():\n75\t    app = _read(\"app.js\")\n76\t    assert 'addEventListener(\"click\"' in app, \"app.js must wire clicks via event delegation\"\n77\t    assert \"crypto.subtle\" in app and \"Ed25519\" in app, \"app.js must use WebCrypto Ed25519\"\n78\t    # honest failure path if the browser cannot hold a device key (no silent weak-crypto fallback)\n79\t    assert \"can't hold a device key\" in app or \"cannot hold a device key\" in app, \\\n80\t        \"app.js must fail honestly when crypto.subtle lacks Ed25519\"\n81\t\n82\t\n83\t# ---- 3. CANONICALIZATION PARITY (the signed-bytes contract), verified under Node ------------------\n84\t_NODE_SCRIPT = (\n85\t    \"const {canonicalJson}=require(process.env.CANON);\"\n86\t    \"const core=JSON.parse(process.argv[1]);\"\n87\t    \"process.stdout.write(Buffer.from(canonicalJson(core),'utf8'));\"\n88\t)\n89\t\n90\t\n91\tdef _node_canonical(core: dict) -> bytes:\n92\t    \"\"\"Run the SHIPPED JS canonicalJson (canonical.js) under Node over `core`; return its UTF-8 bytes.\"\"\"\n93\t    out = subprocess.run(\n94\t        [\"node\", \"-e\", _NODE_SCRIPT, json.dumps(core)],\n95\t        env={\"CANON\": str((WEBAPP / \"canonical.js\").resolve()), \"PATH\": __import__(\"os\").environ.get(\"PATH\", \"\")},\n96\t        capture_output=True, timeout=30,\n97\t    )\n98\t    assert out.returncode == 0, f\"node canonicalJson failed: {out.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}\"\n99\t    return out.stdout\n100\t\n101\t\n102\tdef test_canonicaljson_parity_via_node():\n103\t    if not shutil.which(\"node\"):\n104\t        print(\"  SKIP  node not present — canonicalization parity NOT verified (install Node 22 to falsify)\")\n105\t        return\n106\t\n107\t    # (a) the DOCUMENTED fixed envelope vector — byte-identical to sigil.bridge.envelope.envelope_message\n108\t    core = build_core(\"DEVKEYB64\", \"read:snapshot\", {}, 1, 1700000000)\n109\t    expected = b'{\"action\":\"read:snapshot\",\"args\":{},\"device\":\"DEVKEYB64\",\"nonce\":1,\"ts\":1700000000,\"v\":1}'\n110\t    assert envelope_message(core) == expected, \"the Python parity contract byte string drifted\"\n111\t    js = _node_canonical(core)\n112\t    assert js == expected, f\"JS canonicalJson drifted from the pinned vector:\\n  py={expected!r}\\n  js={js!r}\"\n113\t    assert js == envelope_message(core), \"JS canonicalJson != Python envelope_message (signatures would be rejected)\"\n114\t\n115\t    # (b) the approval message the phone signs for /api/action — canonical_json({approver,decision,target})\n116\t    approval = {\"approver\": \"device\", \"decision\": \"approved\", \"target\": 5}\n117\t    assert _node_canonical(approval) == canonical_json(approval), \"approval-message canonicalization drifted\"\n118\t\n119\t    # (c) nested / unicode / integer edges — key sort recurses, non-ASCII stays raw, ints have no .0\n120\t    for obj in (\n121\t        {\"b\": 2, \"a\": {\"z\": [3, 2, 1], \"y\": \"x\"}, \"n\": None, \"t\": True, \"f\": False},\n122\t        {\"device\": \"abc/def+ghi==\", \"note\": \"café — naïve ✓\", \"nonce\": 42},\n123\t        {\"args\": {\"text\": \"halt now\"}, \"action\": \"relay\", \"v\": 1, \"nonce\": 7, \"ts\": 1700000123, \"device\": \"K\"},\n124\t    ):\n125\t        assert _node_canonical(obj) == canonical_json(obj), f\"canonicalization parity failed for {obj!r}\"\n126\t\n127\t\n128\tif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n129\t    fns = [v for k, v in sorted(globals().items()) if k.startswith(\"test_\")]\n130\t    passed = 0\n131\t    for fn in fns:\n132\t        try:\n133\t            fn(); print(f\"  PASS  {fn.__name__}\"); passed += 1\n134\t        except AssertionError as e:\n135\t            print(f\"  FAIL  {fn.__name__}: {e}\")\n136\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n137\t            import traceback\n138\t            print(f\"  ERROR {fn.__name__}: {e}\")\n139\t            traceback.print_exc()\n140\t    print(f\"{passed}/{len(fns)} Phase-9 W1-C (Companion PWA) guarantees hold\")\n141\t"}]},"uuid":"9e5cea66-2572-4802-b620-2ac91c8f6ea2","timestamp":"2026-07-19T05:27:45.517Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"36c3a83b-00ff-4620-ad27-97f3247bf81d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
{"parentUuid":"e6b40c2f-601b-498b-9e95-7fe75c49c8e1","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"49872cc4-d709-4ab4-ae05-cf02560ec711","agentId":"a24ebe54d96b84494","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Ccn1CH7XFTg5pxaGo1UnAs","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The SIGIL bridge server (Phase 9 W1-B) — the WireGuard-bound HTTP transport that lets an\n2\tAUTHORIZED phone reach the desktop `BridgeDaemon`. It forks the WS-C glass-cockpit server\n3\t(`sigil.ui.server`) verbatim in shape (ThreadingHTTPServer + BaseHTTPRequestHandler, the strict\n4\tCSP/nosniff/no-referrer header set, the body cap + 30s timeout, the never-log-auth `log_message`,\n5\tthe SSE structure, the anti-DNS-rebinding Host/Origin/Referer gate) and changes ONLY three things:\n6\t\n7\t  • THE BIND. It binds a `bind_ok` address (loopback or a PRIVATE/WireGuard address) — NEVER\n8\t    0.0.0.0 / a public address. The constructor asserts this; the CLI asserts it too. This is the\n9\t    non-negotiable exposure guard: the tunnel, not the transport, is the network boundary.\n10\t\n11\t  • THE AUTH. There is NO wire bearer secret (the ui's printed token is gone). Authentication IS a\n12\t    per-request Ed25519 signature the phone makes with ITS OWN owner-authorized device key — the\n13\t    Wave-1 device envelope (`bridge.envelope`). The server verifies the signature against the\n14\t    owner-minted authorized-device set (recomputed PER REQUEST so a revocation takes effect at once),\n15\t    binds the authenticated envelope `action` to the endpoint it hit (a `read:pending` envelope can\n16\t    never reach the more-sensitive `read:recall`), applies a wallclock timestamp-freshness window\n17\t    (injectable clock), and for EFFECTFUL actions (panic/relay) additionally runs the envelope's\n18\t    strict monotonic-nonce replay gate (`consume(effectful=True)`). The owner trust-root is NEVER used\n19\t    to sign anything here — the phone signs, the server only verifies.\n20\t\n21\t  • THE ALLOWLIST. The anti-rebind Host/Origin allowlist is derived from the REAL bound address (plus\n22\t    the loopback pair when bound to loopback, for dev), not a hardcoded 127.0.0.1.\n23\t\n24\tEverything sensitive stays off the minimal frames: `/api/pending` and the SSE stream carry only\n25\t`{seq, tier, kind}` — never a subject, never a payload, never a secret. `serve()` now wraps the\n26\ttransport in an owner-PINNED self-signed TLS cert (the phone PWA needs a secure context — https or\n27\tlocalhost — to install and register a service worker; over a bare WireGuard IP that means self-signed\n28\tTLS whose sha256 fingerprint the owner pins once, stable across restarts). `build_server` itself\n29\tstays plain HTTP so the in-tunnel test harness is unchanged and TLS can be terminated upstream if\n30\tpreferred. Offense-free.\"\"\"\n31\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n32\t\n33\timport base64\n34\timport ipaddress\n35\timport json\n36\timport os\n37\timport time\n38\tfrom http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer\n39\tfrom pathlib import Path\n40\tfrom urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse\n41\t\n42\tfrom ..config import SPINE_PATH\n43\tfrom ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n44\tfrom ..mesh import authorized_devices\n45\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n46\tfrom ..spine.verify import verify_record\n47\tfrom .daemon import BridgeDaemon, bind_ok\n48\tfrom .envelope import consume, verify_envelope\n49\tfrom .notifier import PushNotifier\n50\t\n51\t_WEBAPP = Path(__file__).parent / \"webapp\"       # the PWA is a later slice — served if present, else 404\n52\t_CSP = \"default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'\"\n53\t_DEFAULT_PORT = 8722\n54\t_TS_WINDOW = 120.0                               # ± seconds a request timestamp may differ from the server clock\n55\t\n56\t# Each network endpoint declares the ONE envelope action that authorizes it. Binding the\n57\t# authenticated action to the endpoint stops a captured lesser-scoped envelope (e.g. `read:pending`,\n58\t# which leaks only {seq,tier,kind}) from being replayed against a more-sensitive endpoint (e.g.\n59\t# `read:recall`, which surfaces the owner's on-screen OCR history). `/api/graph` piggybacks on the\n60\t# `read:snapshot` scope: graph returns only aggregate health, strictly LESS sensitive than the\n61\t# snapshot, so a snapshot-scoped envelope reaching it is not an escalation (and a lesser envelope\n62\t# still cannot reach it).\n63\t_READ_ACTION = {\n64\t    \"/api/pending\": \"read:pending\",\n65\t    \"/api/snapshot\": \"read:snapshot\",\n66\t    \"/api/graph\": \"read:snapshot\",\n67\t    \"/api/stream\": \"read:stream\",\n68\t    \"/api/recall\": \"read:recall\",\n69\t}\n70\t\n71\t\n72\tclass BridgeServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):\n73\t    daemon_threads = True\n74\t\n75\t    def __init__(self, addr, handler, *, spine_path, trusted_pubkey=None, clock=None,\n76\t                 ts_window: float = _TS_WINDOW):\n77\t        host = addr[0]\n78\t        if not bind_ok(host):\n79\t            raise ValueError(\n80\t                f\"refusing to bind {host!r}: the bridge binds loopback or a PRIVATE (WireGuard) \"\n81\t                f\"address only — never 0.0.0.0 / an unspecified / a public address\")\n82\t        super().__init__(addr, handler)\n83\t        self.spine_path = Path(spine_path)\n84\t        # the owner PUBLIC key is the trust anchor (injectable for tests); NO private key ever lives here\n85\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n86\t        self.clock = clock or time.time          # injectable wallclock so the freshness gate is deterministic\n87\t        self.ts_window = ts_window\n88\t        port = self.server_address[1]            # the ACTUAL bound port (correct even for port 0)\n89\t        hosts = {f\"{host}:{port}\"}\n90\t        origins = {f\"http://{host}:{port}\"}\n91\t        if ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback:   # dev convenience only — not added for a WG bind\n92\t            hosts |= {f\"127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"localhost:{port}\"}\n93\t            origins |= {f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"http://localhost:{port}\"}\n94\t        self.allowed_hosts = frozenset(hosts)\n95\t        self.allowed_origins = frozenset(origins)\n96\t\n97\t    def store(self) -> SpineStore:\n98\t        return SpineStore(self.spine_path)       # fresh read each request (cheap, current)\n99\t\n100\t    def daemon(self) -> BridgeDaemon:\n101\t        return BridgeDaemon(self.store(), trusted_pubkey=self.trusted_pubkey)\n102\t\n103\t\n104\tdef _json_bytes(obj) -> bytes:\n105\t    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")\n106\t\n107\t\n108\tclass Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):\n109\t    server_version = \"sigil-bridge/1.0\"\n110\t    timeout = 30                                  # per-connection socket timeout (no hung reader)\n111\t    _MAX_BODY = 65536                             # bodies are tiny; cap to avoid a Content-Length hang/alloc\n112\t\n113\t    # never log auth (an envelope can ride in ?env= for SSE; never write it to a log)\n114\t    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # noqa: A003\n115\t        pass\n116\t\n117\t    # --- request helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n118\t    def _query(self) -> dict:\n119\t        return parse_qs(urlparse(self.path).query)\n120\t\n121\t    def _authorized_now(self):\n122\t        \"\"\"The owner-minted authorized-device set, recomputed PER REQUEST — a revoke takes effect now.\"\"\"\n123\t        return authorized_devices(self.server.store(), self.server.trusted_pubkey)\n124\t\n125\t    def _envelope_payload(self):\n126\t        \"\"\"The device envelope: base64url of canonical JSON, in `X-SIGIL-Envelope` (GET/POST) or the\n127\t        `?env=` query (SSE, which cannot set a header). Returns the payload dict, or None if absent/\n128\t        malformed (fail-closed — the caller denies).\"\"\"\n129\t        raw = self.headers.get(\"X-SIGIL-Envelope\") or (self._query().get(\"env\", [\"\"])[0])\n130\t        if not raw:\n131\t            return None\n132\t        try:\n133\t            data = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw + \"=\" * (-len(raw) % 4))\n134\t            payload = json.loads(data)\n135\t        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — any decode/parse failure is an unauthenticated request\n136\t            return None\n137\t        return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None\n138\t\n139\t    def _fresh(self, core) -> bool:\n140\t        \"\"\"The server-layer wallclock freshness window (the envelope module is pure — it never reads a\n141\t        clock — so freshness lives HERE). A non-numeric / far-off timestamp fails closed.\"\"\"\n142\t        try:\n143\t            ts = float(core.get(\"ts\"))\n144\t        except (TypeError, ValueError):\n145\t            return False\n146\t        return abs(self.server.clock() - ts) <= self.server.ts_window\n147\t\n148\t    def _authed(self, action: str):\n149\t        \"\"\"Authenticate a READ: verify the device signature, apply freshness, bind the action to this\n150\t        endpoint. Reads are side-effect-free, so they are NOT receipted (no spine write per GET) — the\n151\t        freshness window is their replay bound. Returns the core, or None after sending a deny.\"\"\"\n152\t        payload = self._envelope_payload()\n153\t        if payload is None:\n154\t            self._deny(401, \"missing/invalid device envelope\")\n155\t            return None\n156\t        ok, core = verify_envelope(payload, self._authorized_now())\n157\t        if not ok:\n158\t            self._deny(401, f\"unauthenticated: {core}\")\n159\t            return None\n160\t        if not self._fresh(core):\n161\t            self._deny(401, \"stale request (timestamp outside freshness window)\")\n162\t            return None\n163\t        if core.get(\"action\") != action:\n164\t            self._deny(403, \"envelope action does not authorize this endpoint\")\n165\t            return None\n166\t        return core\n167\t\n168\t    def _authed_effectful(self, action: str):\n169\t        \"\"\"Authenticate an EFFECTFUL request (panic/relay): verify + freshness + endpoint-bind, then run\n170\t        the envelope's strict monotonic-nonce replay gate and receipt it on the spine\n171\t        (`consume(effectful=True)`). A replayed/stale-nonce envelope is refused. Returns core or None.\"\"\"\n172\t        payload = self._envelope_payload()\n173\t        if payload is None:\n174\t            self._deny(401, \"missing/invalid device envelope\")\n175\t            return None\n176\t        authorized = self._authorized_now()\n177\t        ok, core = verify_envelope(payload, authorized)\n178\t        if not ok:\n179\t            self._deny(401, f\"unauthenticated: {core}\")\n180\t            return None\n181\t        if not self._fresh(core):\n182\t            self._deny(401, \"stale request (timestamp outside freshness window)\")\n183\t            return None\n184\t        if core.get(\"action\") != action:\n185\t            self._deny(403, \"envelope action does not authorize this endpoint\")\n186\t            return None\n187\t        try:\n188\t            return consume(self.server.store(), payload, authorized, effectful=True)\n189\t        except ValueError as e:                   # replay: nonce not fresh (fail-closed)\n190\t            self._deny(409, f\"refused: {str(e)[:120]}\")\n191\t            return None\n192\t\n193\t    def _rebind_ok(self) -> bool:\n194\t        \"\"\"The anti-DNS-rebinding gate (ui `_action_ok` logic, minus the token — the envelope is the\n195\t        credential): the `Host` must be in the WG-derived allowlist, an `Origin`, if present, must\n196\t        EXACT-match an allowed origin (a prefix like `http://IP:PORT.evil.com` must NOT pass), and a\n197\t        `Referer`, if present, must sit under an allowed origin. Applied to the whole POST action\n198\t        plane as defense-in-depth.\"\"\"\n199\t        if self.headers.get(\"Host\", \"\") not in self.server.allowed_hosts:\n200\t            return False\n201\t        o = self.headers.get(\"Origin\") or \"\"\n202\t        ref = self.headers.get(\"Referer\") or \"\"\n203\t        if o and o not in self.server.allowed_origins:\n204\t            return False\n205\t        if ref and not any(ref.startswith(a + \"/\") or ref == a for a in self.server.allowed_origins):\n206\t            return False\n207\t        return True\n208\t\n209\t    # --- response helpers -------------------------------------------------------------------------\n210\t    def _send(self, code: int, body: bytes, ctype=\"application/json\"):\n211\t        self.send_response(code)\n212\t        self.send_header(\"Content-Type\", ctype)\n213\t        self.send_header(\"Content-Length\", str(len(body)))\n214\t        self.send_header(\"Content-Security-Policy\", _CSP)\n215\t        self.send_header(\"X-Content-Type-Options\", \"nosniff\")\n216\t        self.send_header(\"Referrer-Policy\", \"no-referrer\")\n217\t        self.end_headers()\n218\t        try:\n219\t            self.wfile.write(body)\n220\t        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):\n221\t            pass\n222\t\n223\t    def _json(self, obj, code=200):\n224\t        self._send(code, _json_bytes(obj))\n225\t\n226\t    def _deny(self, code=403, msg=\"forbidden\"):\n227\t        self._json({\"error\": msg}, code)\n228\t\n229\t    # --- GET (read plane) -------------------------------------------------------------------------\n230\t    def do_GET(self):\n231\t        path = urlparse(self.path).path\n232\t        if path in (\"/\", \"/index.html\"):\n233\t            return self._serve_index()\n234\t        if path.startswith(\"/static/\"):\n235\t            return self._serve_static(path[len(\"/static/\"):])\n236\t        if not path.startswith(\"/api/\"):\n237\t            return self._deny(404, \"not found\")\n238\t        if path == \"/api/stream\":\n239\t            return self._sse()                    # SSE authenticates via ?env= inside _authed\n240\t        if path == \"/api/pending\":\n241\t            if self._authed(_READ_ACTION[path]) is None:\n242\t                return\n243\t            return self._json({\"pending\": self.server.daemon().pending()})   # {seq,tier,kind} only\n244\t        if path == \"/api/snapshot\":\n245\t            if self._authed(_READ_ACTION[path]) is None:\n246\t                return\n247\t            from ..dashboard import snapshot\n248\t            return self._json(snapshot(self.server.store()))\n249\t        if path == \"/api/graph\":\n250\t            if self._authed(_READ_ACTION[path]) is None:\n251\t                return\n252\t            return self._graph()\n253\t        if path.startswith(\"/api/record/\"):\n254\t            if self._authed(\"read:record\") is None:\n255\t                return\n256\t            return self._record(path.rsplit(\"/\", 1)[-1])\n257\t        if path == \"/api/recall\":\n258\t            if self._authed(_READ_ACTION[path]) is None:\n259\t                return\n260\t            subject = self._query().get(\"subject\", [\"\"])[0]\n261\t            return self._json({\"subject\": subject, \"recall\": self.server.daemon().recall(subject)})\n262\t        return self._deny(404, \"unknown endpoint\")\n263\t\n264\t    def _serve_index(self):\n265\t        idx = _WEBAPP / \"index.html\"\n266\t        if not idx.is_file():\n267\t            return self._deny(404, \"bridge PWA not built yet\")   # graceful — the webapp is a later slice\n268\t        try:\n269\t            self._send(200, idx.read_bytes(), ctype=\"text/html; charset=utf-8\")\n270\t        except OSError:\n271\t            self._deny(404, \"not found\")\n272\t\n273\t    def _serve_static(self, sub: str):\n274\t        base = _WEBAPP.resolve()\n275\t        target = (base / sub).resolve()\n276\t        if base != target and base not in target.parents:        # traversal guard (allowlist by containment)\n277\t            return self._deny(404, \"not found\")\n278\t        if not target.is_file():\n279\t            return self._deny(404, \"not found\")                  # includes: webapp dir absent (later slice)\n280\t        name = target.name\n281\t        ctype = (\"application/javascript\" if name.endswith(\".js\")\n282\t                 else \"text/css\" if name.endswith(\".css\")\n283\t                 else \"text/html\" if name.endswith(\".html\")\n284\t                 else \"application/octet-stream\")\n285\t        try:\n286\t            self._send(200, target.read_bytes(), ctype=f\"{ctype}; charset=utf-8\")\n287\t        except OSError:\n288\t            self._deny(404, \"not found\")\n289\t\n290\t    def _record(self, raw):\n291\t        try:\n292\t            seq = int(raw)\n293\t        except ValueError:\n294\t            return self._deny(400, \"bad seq\")\n295\t        rec = self.server.store().get(seq)\n296\t        if rec is None:\n297\t            return self._json({\"error\": \"no such record\", \"seq\": seq,\n298\t                               \"note\": \"no grounded record — not fabricated\"}, 404)\n299\t        ok, reason = verify_record(rec)                          # re-verify the atom LIVE (prove-don't-guess)\n300\t        self._json({\"seq\": rec.seq, \"kind\": rec.kind, \"source\": rec.source, \"actor\": rec.actor,\n301\t                    \"ts\": rec.ts, \"entry_hash\": rec.entry_hash, \"prev_hash\": rec.prev_hash,\n302\t                    \"payload\": rec.payload, \"integrity_ok\": ok, \"integrity_reason\": reason})\n303\t\n304\t    def _graph(self):\n305\t        try:\n306\t            from ..graph import health\n307\t            self._json({\"health\": health()})\n308\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — graph may not be built yet (ImportError included)\n309\t            self._json({\"error\": \"graph unavailable\", \"note\": str(e)[:200]})\n310\t\n311\t    def _sse(self):\n312\t        if self._authed(\"read:stream\") is None:                  # deny already sent (401/403)\n313\t            return\n314\t        self.send_response(200)\n315\t        self.send_header(\"Content-Type\", \"text/event-stream\")\n316\t        self.send_header(\"Cache-Control\", \"no-cache\")\n317\t        self.send_header(\"Content-Security-Policy\", _CSP)\n318\t        self.send_header(\"X-Content-Type-Options\", \"nosniff\")\n319\t        self.send_header(\"Referrer-Policy\", \"no-referrer\")\n320\t        self.end_headers()\n321\t        try:\n322\t            since = int(self._query().get(\"since\", [\"-1\"])[0])\n323\t        except (ValueError, TypeError):\n324\t            since = -1                                            # any malformed cursor → from genesis\n325\t        notifier = PushNotifier(self.server.store(), since_seq=since)\n326\t        try:\n327\t            while True:\n328\t                sent = False\n329\t                for ev in notifier.poll():\n330\t                    frame = {\"seq\": ev[\"seq\"], \"tier\": ev[\"tier\"], \"kind\": ev[\"kind\"]}   # minimal — no subject\n331\t                    self.wfile.write(f\"data: {json.dumps(frame, ensure_ascii=False)}\\n\\n\".encode(\"utf-8\"))\n332\t                    sent = True\n333\t                self.wfile.write(b\": hb\\n\\n\")                     # heartbeat / flush\n334\t                self.wfile.flush()\n335\t                if not sent:\n336\t                    time.sleep(0.25)\n337\t        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError, OSError):\n338\t            return                                                # client closed — end the stream\n339\t\n340\t    # --- POST (action plane) ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n341\t    def do_POST(self):\n342\t        path = urlparse(self.path).path\n343\t        if path not in (\"/api/action\", \"/api/panic\", \"/api/relay\", \"/api/gesture/arm\"):\n344\t            return self._deny(404, \"not found\")\n345\t        length = int(self.headers.get(\"Content-Length\", \"0\") or \"0\")\n346\t        if length > self._MAX_BODY:                              # cap the body (no CL hang / alloc)\n347\t            return self._deny(413, \"body too large\")\n348\t        body_bytes = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b\"\"\n349\t        if not self._rebind_ok():                               # anti-rebind gate on the whole action plane\n350\t            return self._deny(403, \"action denied (origin / host — possible DNS rebinding)\")\n351\t        if path == \"/api/action\":\n352\t            return self._device_action(body_bytes)\n353\t        if path == \"/api/gesture/arm\":\n354\t            return self._device_arm(body_bytes)\n355\t        # panic / relay — effectful, envelope-authenticated with the strict nonce replay gate\n356\t        action = \"panic\" if path == \"/api/panic\" else \"relay\"\n357\t        core = self._authed_effectful(action)\n358\t        if core is None:\n359\t            return\n360\t        if action == \"panic\":\n361\t            return self._json({\"ok\": True, \"seq\": self.server.daemon().panic_engage(by=\"phone\")})\n362\t        text = str((core.get(\"args\") or {}).get(\"text\", \"\"))     # the relayed command is INSIDE the signed core\n363\t        return self._json({\"ok\": True, \"reply\": self.server.daemon().relay(text)})\n364\t\n365\t    def _device_action(self, body_bytes):\n366\t        \"\"\"The phone posts its OWN device-signed `governor.approval` payload. The SERVER only VERIFIES\n367\t        (it never signs) — `submit_device_approval` accepts it iff the signing device is currently\n368\t        authorized AND the signature verifies; the signed `target_seq` binds, so no nonce is needed.\"\"\"\n369\t        try:\n370\t            body = json.loads(body_bytes or b\"{}\")\n371\t        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:\n372\t            return self._deny(400, f\"bad request: {e}\")\n373\t        if not isinstance(body, dict):\n374\t            return self._deny(400, \"bad request: body must be a JSON object\")\n375\t        try:\n376\t            seq = self.server.daemon().submit_device_approval(body)\n377\t        except ValueError as e:                                  # unauthorized / forged / not-an-approval\n378\t            return self._deny(403, f\"approval refused: {str(e)[:200]}\")\n379\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — never leak internals as a 500\n380\t            return self._deny(400, f\"action failed: {str(e)[:200]}\")\n381\t        self._json({\"ok\": True, \"seq\": seq})\n382\t\n383\t    def _device_arm(self, body_bytes):\n384\t        \"\"\"The phone posts its OWN device-signed gesture arm request. The SERVER only VERIFIES + RECORDS\n385\t        it (`submit_arm_request`, fail-closed on unauthorized/forged); the live SessionGate re-verifies\n386\t        and enforces freshness / kill-switch / single-session / TTL when it consumes it. Recording is\n387\t        necessary-but-not-sufficient to arm — the trust boundary is `arm_by_device`, not this endpoint.\"\"\"\n388\t        try:\n389\t            body = json.loads(body_bytes or b\"{}\")\n390\t        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:\n391\t            return self._deny(400, f\"bad request: {e}\")\n392\t        if not isinstance(body, dict):\n393\t            return self._deny(400, \"bad request: body must be a JSON object\")\n394\t        try:\n395\t            seq = self.server.daemon().submit_arm_request(body)\n396\t        except ValueError as e:                                  # unauthorized / forged / not-an-arm-request\n397\t            return self._deny(403, f\"arm refused: {str(e)[:200]}\")\n398\t        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — never leak internals as a 500\n399\t            return self._deny(400, f\"arm failed: {str(e)[:200]}\")\n400\t        self._json({\"ok\": True, \"seq\": seq})\n401\t\n402\t\n403\tdef build_server(*, addr: str, port: int = _DEFAULT_PORT, spine_path=None, trusted_pubkey=None,\n404\t                 clock=None) -> BridgeServer:\n405\t    \"\"\"Build (but do not run) the bridge server bound to `addr` (asserted `bind_ok`). `trusted_pubkey`\n406\t    and `clock` are injectable for deterministic tests; both default to the real owner identity / wallclock.\"\"\"\n407\t    return BridgeServer((addr, port), Handler,\n408\t                        spine_path=Path(spine_path) if spine_path else SPINE_PATH,\n409\t                        trusted_pubkey=trusted_pubkey, clock=clock)\n410\t\n411\t\n412\tdef _write_secure(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n413\t    \"\"\"Write `data` to `path` created 0600 up-front (no world-readable window) — the vault/secrets\n414\t    secure-file idiom (`os.open(..., 0o600)`).\"\"\"\n415\t    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)\n416\t    with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as fh:\n417\t        fh.write(data)\n418\t\n419\t\n420\tdef _fingerprint(cert) -> str:\n421\t    \"\"\"The pinned identity: sha256 of the DER cert, hex, colon-grouped byte pairs (openssl-style,\n422\t    upper-case) — what the owner eyeball-matches on the phone once.\"\"\"\n423\t    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes\n424\t    h = cert.fingerprint(hashes.SHA256()).hex().upper()      # fingerprint() == sha256 of the DER encoding\n425\t    return \":\".join(h[i:i + 2] for i in range(0, len(h), 2))\n426\t\n427\t\n428\tdef ensure_bridge_cert(addr: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n429\t    \"\"\"Mint (or REUSE) a minimal owner-pinned self-signed TLS cert for the bridge bound to `addr`,\n430\t    returning `(certfile, keyfile, sha256_fingerprint)`.\n431\t\n432\t    The cert carries `addr` as its CN and (when `addr` is an IP — always true for a `bind_ok` bridge)\n433\t    as an `x509.IPAddress` SubjectAlternativeName, so an IP-literal TLS connection matches. Cert+key\n434\t    live under `SIGIL_HOME/bridge/` (dir 0700, files 0600). If a cert already exists FOR THIS ADDR it\n435\t    is REUSED — the fingerprint is therefore STABLE across restarts, so the owner pins it exactly once\n436\t    (a changed fingerprint later means a MITM / a wiped key, not a benign restart). An EC P-256 key is\n437\t    used (easy for `cryptography`, accepted by `ssl`). The arm-request JS:\n\n```js\nvar ARM_TTL_SECONDS = 120;\nasync function buildArmRequest() {\n  var core = {\n    signal: \"gesture.arm_request\",\n    device_id: DEVICE.deviceId,\n    nonce: await nextNonce(),          // fresh monotonic int, distinct per arm\n    ts: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000), // integer seconds\n    ttl_seconds: ARM_TTL_SECONDS\n  };\n  var sig = await signBytes(enc.encode(SigilCanonical.canonicalJson(core))); // same key/encoding as approvals\n  var body = {};\n  for (var kk in core) { if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(core, kk)) { body[kk] = core[kk]; } }\n  body.pubkey = DEVICE.pubB64;\n  body.sig = sig;\n  return body;\n}\n```\n\n`onArm()` POSTs `{...core, pubkey, sig}` to `/api/gesture/arm` via the existing `deliver(...)` (no `X-SIGIL-Envelope`; `Content-Type: application/json`), then shows the JSON result honestly: on 2xx `{ok,seq}` it renders **\"arm request SENT · recorded at seq N\"** plus copy stating it is **\"not armed yet\"** and that the desktop daemon re-verifies freshness/kill-switch/single-session/TTL and is what actually arms; refusals and the offline-queued case are shown honestly too.\n\n### `sigil/bridge/webapp/index.html`\n- Added `<div id=\"outbox-status\" class=\"mono\"></div>` right under `#banner` (top-of-page, so a failed emergency stop is unmissable).\n- Added an **\"Arm gesture session\"** panel with `<button data-act=\"arm-gesture\" id=\"arm-btn\">` + `#arm-msg`, hint copy noting it records a signed request and the desktop is what actually arms. The sig path reuses `signBytes` → standard base64 with padding, which is exactly what Python `sign`/`verify_one` (`base64.b64decode(validate=True)`) requires, so signatures verify in `submit_arm_request`/`arm_by_device`.\n\nResult: `8/8 Phase-9 W1-C (Companion PWA) guarantees hold`; `node --check app.js` OK.\n\n## Deviations / notes\n- I used a **dedicated `#outbox-status` element** rather than the old `#panic-msg` reuse, because `#panic-msg` is overwritten by `onPanic` and the app-wide `banner` is wiped every ~5s by `authedGet`'s success `clearBanner()` — neither could hold a persistent failure notice.
